# gitmoap_catalog_service_dependents (Data Source)

List the services that depend on this service. Returns each inbound dependency with its kind (package, api or datastore), how it was learned, and the repository whose file established it. A dependent you cannot see is left out but counted, and a very large list is cut short and flagged. Anyone who can see the service may call it.

The token needs `catalog:read`.

## Example Usage

```terraform
data "gitmoap_group_by_path" "platform" {
  full_path = "acme/platform"
}

resource "gitmoap_catalog_service" "api" {
  group_id = data.gitmoap_group_by_path.platform.group_id
  slug     = "api"
  external = true
}

data "gitmoap_catalog_service_dependents" "example" {
  service_id = gitmoap_catalog_service.api.service_id
}
```

<!-- schema generated by tfplugindocs -->
## Schema

### Required

- `service_id` (String) The service's id

### Read-Only

- `edges` (Attributes List) (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--edges))
- `hidden` (Number) Dependencies left out because you cannot see the service at the far end.
- `truncated` (Boolean) Whether the list stopped at its limit of 500 and more exist.

<a id="nestedatt--edges"></a>
### Nested Schema for `edges`

Read-Only:

- `confidence` (Number) How certain the dependency is: `1.0` for anything the platform observed or a person stated,
lower only for a derived one.
- `detail` (Attributes) Where an observed dependency came from: the package, the versions requested and resolved, and the
lockfile that records it. Absent for a declared dependency, which names none of these. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--edges--detail))
- `from_service_id` (String)
- `kind` (String) How a service depends on the far end of a dependency — not what the far end is. The same
`library` service can be consumed as a package by one service and called over HTTP by another.
- `observed_at` (String)
- `observed_repo` (String)
- `observed_sha` (String)
- `source` (String) How a dependency came to be known, and therefore how far it can be trusted. A declared and an
observed dependency between the same two services are reported separately, so a declaration no
lockfile mentions, or a lockfile entry nobody declared, stands out.
- `to` (Attributes) The short form of a service that listings, search results and path lookups show. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--edges--to))

<a id="nestedatt--edges--detail"></a>
### Nested Schema for `edges.detail`

Read-Only:

- `format` (String) The package ecosystem a registry speaks. A group has at most one registry per format.
- `lockfile_path` (String)
- `package_name` (String)
- `resolved` (String) The version the lockfile actually pins.
- `version_req` (String) What the manifest asked for, where the lockfile records it.


<a id="nestedatt--edges--to"></a>
### Nested Schema for `edges.to`

Read-Only:

- `display_name` (String)
- `external` (Boolean)
- `group_id` (String)
- `kind` (String) What sort of thing a service is. The kind decides which scorecard checks apply: a `library` has
no deployments, so a deployment check is not applicable to it rather than failing. For your own
classifications, use annotations.
- `lifecycle` (String) Where a service is in its life.
- `orphaned_at` (String)
- `owner` (Attributes) Who owns a service: a group, a team, or a person or service account. A service may also have no
owner, which the `has_owner` scorecard check surfaces.

`kind` says which applies: `group`, with `full_path`, `group_id`; `principal`, with `actor`, `principal_id`; `team`, with `organization`, `slug`, `team_id`. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--edges--to--owner))
- `service_id` (String)
- `slug` (String)
- `source` (String) How the catalog entry came to exist. Set by the platform, never accepted from a request. Any
source other than `inferred` means a person has vouched for the entry.

<a id="nestedatt--edges--to--owner"></a>
### Nested Schema for `edges.to.owner`

Read-Only:

- `actor` (Attributes) Who did something — a person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — with what a
client needs to draw and link them, so a page of records names its actors without a lookup each. (see [below for nested schema](#nestedatt--edges--to--owner--actor))
- `full_path` (String)
- `group_id` (String)
- `kind` (String)
- `organization` (String) The full path of the organization's top-level group, such as `acme`.
- `principal_id` (String)
- `slug` (String) The team's slug, such as `backend`.
- `team_id` (String)

<a id="nestedatt--edges--to--owner--actor"></a>
### Nested Schema for `edges.to.owner.actor`

Read-Only:

- `avatar_url` (String) The principal's picture, when one is known. Absent otherwise: a client derives the
deterministic avatar URL itself.
- `email` (String) The principal's address. An agent's is a generated no-reply address — the author of its
commits. `unknown` on a deleted actor and empty on a redacted one.
- `id` (String) The principal's id: a user id, a service account id or an agent id, as `kind` says. Empty on
a redacted actor.
- `kind` (String) A person, a service account or an AI organization's agent — which of the three a principal is,
and so which page it links to: a person's profile, a service account's page or an agent's page.
- `username` (String) The name to show: a person's or service account's username, or an agent's handle (which
always ends in `-ai`). `deleted-user` when the actor no longer resolves, `redacted` when the
caller may not see who it was. A closed account whose work stays is `closed-` and twelve hex
digits, a shape no open account may take, with an address under `.invalid`.
